acceptance: 1) Caller/wiring point: the three visitor handlers -> cookie-scoped service. Reads are owner-only and seq-ascending with a maximum page size of 100. With concurrent inserts between pages, catch-up contains each message ID once. Read cursors advance by MAX only to an existing seq; synchronization does not automatically mark messages read (E-19, E-34, E-77, E-79). 2) Appending a message locks the row, increments seq, and commits with the outbox. The same UUID/payload retried after response loss returns the original id/seq; a changed payload returns 409. Closed/anonymized conversations reject writes. Unknown outcomes use bounded retries with the original key, not a new key (E-18, E-33, E-37). 3) Actual expired/revoked cookies fail the next read and write; the same email cannot restore authority. GET/read renew neither seven-day idle nor 90-day content retention. Cookie expiry does not delete consultations still within 90 days; authorized operators can still handle them (E-78, E-85, E-86, E-89).

E-18.trigger: The same message is submitted repeatedly because of retries.
E-18.expect: Deduplicate by the client message identifier so the inbox contains one message and notifications are not triggered repeatedly.

E-19.trigger: A visitor guesses another conversation identifier, or an unauthorized admin account accesses the inbox.
E-19.expect: Reject reads and replies. A visitor may access only their own conversation using their own unguessable session credential.

E-33.scene: C-01 Human inbox and reply entry points
E-33.trigger: Two authorized people reply concurrently, or a visitor repeats the same client message identifier.
E-33.expect: Order by server seq and show the actual author. The same clientMessageId and payload in the same conversation produce only one message, one outbox item, and one unread increment. Persist each concurrent human reply; a later response must not overwrite an earlier saved reply.

E-34.scene: C-01 Human inbox and reply entry points
E-34.trigger: A new message arrives while the inbox is refreshed or paginated.
E-34.expect: Apply the defined seq cursor and read MAX rules: insert messages between pages and verify that each message ID in the completed range appears exactly once. Advance read only to the seq actually confirmed by the user; newly arrived higher-seq messages remain unread.

E-37.scene: C-02 Offline messages and recovery from send failures
E-37.trigger: Submission times out or the response is lost, leaving actual persistence unknown.
E-37.expect: Show a confirmation-pending or retryable state. Retry with the original client message identifier and return the original receipt result, without duplicating inbox or notification items.

E-77.trigger: There are multiple tabs, retries, out-of-order responses, or new messages inserted between pages.
E-77.expect: Merge and deduplicate by stable server seq and message identifier. Advance the cursor only through the fully received range. A late old response must not move the cursor backward, overwrite a newer reply, or skip messages on an omitted page.

E-78.trigger: A visitor session expires or is revoked, or an operator loses chat permission after previously holding ADMIN/SALES.
E-78.expect: Perform server-side authorization on the next poll and send, and stop returning conversation content. Changing threadId, seq, or email cannot read another consultation.

E-79.trigger: The network recovers after an interruption, or the operator inbox has many unread messages.
E-79.expect: Bind bounded pages to the established pagination cap, verify that no request exceeds it, and continuously fill seq gaps. Polling updates only the confirmed-receipt cursor, not the user's read position, and must not create an operator-online or read promise.

E-85.trigger: The cookie reaches seven idle days or 30 days since issuance, or is revoked.
E-85.expect: The server rejects access to the old conversation using that credential; the browser may start a new consultation. Re-entering the same email alone cannot restore the old conversation. Neither the cookie nor any frontend copy stores PII.

E-86.trigger: A hidden tab still polls, or a visit merely refreshes without successfully sending or receiving a consultation message.
E-86.expect: These behaviors do not postpone the 90-day retention deadline for messages/email. Consultation activity means successfully persisted visitor messages or human replies; notification retries, delivery receipts, and read-state updates do not count as new consultation activity.

E-89.trigger: A chat cookie becomes invalid while the messages are still within 90 days.
E-89.expect: Immediately block the visitor's historical access. Operators can still process retained consultations under existing ADMIN/SALES authorization. Do not implicitly change the existing 730-day inquiry, 30-day/13-month analytics, or backup policies.
